summary: The change passes the listed suite but still overflows the stack for large literals containing a long internal run of spaces, so it does not meet the main requirement. It also appends a quote to unmatched apostrophes, changing text outside recognized literal pairs.

findings.claim: Flushing a long run of spaces with spread still exceeds the JavaScript argument limit. A literal with 200,000 internal spaces followed by a nonspace character throws RangeError; a 15 million character literal of this form cannot complete.

The scanner unconditionally adds a closing quote when an opening apostrophe has no matching quote, altering SQL comments and other text outside recognized quote pairs. The previous implementation preserved that text.
findings.repro: node --input-type=module -e "import {trimLiterals} from './tools/sql-literals.mjs'; console.log(trimLiterals(\"INSERT INTO t VALUES ('x  ') -- it's done\"));"
